question: Why is double-checking (validating) your data such an important step in assessment?

options.A: It is required by law to be completed within fifteen minutes of admission
options.B: It allows the nurse to delegate all future care tasks to unlicensed staff
options.C: It ensures your information is correct before you make clinical choices
options.D: It completely eliminates the need for any subjective patient interviews

explanation: Validating helps you catch mix-ups or misunderstandings early, so you don't build a care plan on the wrong information. Always good to double-check! [learn more](GNS123_U4_T7#GNS123_U4_T7_h2)

question: If a patient loses their pulse, what document should you check right away to see if they didn't want life-saving efforts?

options.A: Patient admission summary
options.B: Do Not Resuscitate order
options.C: Daily nursing care plan
options.D: Discharge planning form

explanation: Great thinking! A DNR order tells the team whether the patient requested to skip measures like CPR. [learn more](GNS221_U4_T9#GNS221_U4_T9_h2)

question: A patient twists their ankle and cannot take four steps without severe pain. What is the best next step?

options.A: Assess for bone tenderness and prepare the patient for a possible X-ray
options.B: Apply a warm compress immediately to relax the joint muscles
options.C: Discharge the patient home with instructions for strict bed rest only
options.D: Massage the ankle firmly to check for deep ligament tears

explanation: When a patient can't bear weight after an injury, standard safety guidelines require checking for bone tenderness and getting an X-ray to rule out a fracture. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T9#GNS222_U1_T9_h3)

question: What is the main role of thrombin in the common pathway?

options.A: It prevents blood from clotting inside healthy vessels
options.B: It destroys excess platelets before they can form a plug
options.C: It causes smooth muscle in the vessel wall to relax
options.D: It converts soluble fibrinogen into insoluble fibrin strands

explanation: Thrombin acts as the key enzyme that turns liquid fibrinogen into solid fibrin threads to build the actual clot structure. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T3#GNS111_U2_T3_h4)

question: Which of these is a key responsibility for a nurse working in public health cancer advocacy?

options.A: Organizing community awareness and teaching early detection methods
options.B: Diagnosing cancer stages without the need for pathology reports
options.C: Performing independent surgical removal of malignant tumors
options.D: Manufacturing chemotherapy medications in hospital pharmacies

explanation: Brilliant! Nurses play a leading role in public health by educating communities, spreading awareness, and encouraging early screening. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T3#GNS321_U1_T3_h7)

question: How should a nurse approach a physical assessment for a patient with a history of FGM?

options.A: Perform the examination quickly without discussing the steps to save time.
options.B: Avoid performing any physical examinations to prevent patient anxiety.
options.C: Explain every step gently and proceed with high sensitivity.
options.D: Ask family members to hold the patient still during the assessment.

explanation: Trauma-informed care is everything here! Clear communication, asking for consent, and gentle handling help rebuild trust with your patient. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T3#GNS312_U1_T3_h7)

question: How many minutes of moderate-intensity aerobic exercise are generally recommended per week for cardiovascular health?

options.A: At least 75 minutes
options.B: At least 150 minutes
options.C: At least 500 minutes
options.D: At least 300 minutes

explanation: Standard health guidelines recommend a minimum of 150 minutes of moderate aerobic activity weekly to maintain heart health and lower disease risk. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T15#GNS213_U1_T15_h4)

question: Why does rapid international travel pose a major risk during an outbreak?

options.A: It allows a local pathogen to spread globally in hours
options.B: It prevents local clinics from ordering basic supplies
options.C: It automatically destroys the genetic code of medications
options.D: It forces travelers to abandon all personal hygiene habits

explanation: Fast global movement means an infected person can board a plane while healthy and land in another country before showing symptoms. [learn more](GNS123_U4_T5#GNS123_U4_T5_h2)

question: What happens to blood vessels as a person ages normally?

options.A: Complete disappearance of capillary beds
options.B: Rapid dilation and excessive blood pooling
options.C: Spontaneous regeneration of damaged valves
options.D: Loss of elasticity and increased stiffness

explanation: You got it! Over time, blood vessels lose their stretchy fibers, becoming stiffer, which naturally contributes to higher blood pressure in older adults. [learn more](GNS321_U3_T2#GNS321_U3_T2_h2)

question: What is the main problem when a drug loses its strength because of bad storage?

options.A: Rapid expiration of hospital staff
options.B: Treatment failure for the patient
options.C: Immediate toxic shock in the ward
options.D: Immediate change in tablet color

explanation: When drugs lose their potency, they simply won't work to heal the patient, leading to poor recovery. Always make sure storage conditions are right! [learn more](GNS125_U4_T4#GNS125_U4_T4_h1)

question: Why do large family sizes still hold a lot of cultural importance in many Nigerian communities?

options.A: Government policies mandate a minimum number of children per household.
options.B: Modern contraceptives are completely unavailable in rural areas.
options.C: They are viewed as a symbol of wealth and ancestral continuity.
options.D: Traditional healers require large families for spiritual protection.

explanation: Exactly! In many traditional settings, having a large family is celebrated as a sign of prosperity, strength, and keeping the family lineage alive. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T003#GNS226_U6_T003_h2)

question: Which hormone tells the Leydig cells in the testes to produce testosterone?

options.A: Gonadotropin-releasing hormone
options.B: Follicle-stimulating hormone
options.C: Luteinizing hormone
options.D: Thyroid-stimulating hormone

explanation: Spot on! Luteinizing hormone (LH) comes from the anterior pituitary gland and travels down to tell the Leydig cells to make testosterone. You've got this! [learn more](GNS311_U1_T9#GNS311_U1_T9_h1)

question: What is one of the most important nursing duties when caring for a patient with a GI disorder?

options.A: Performing independent endoscopy exams
options.B: Tracking exact fluid intake and output
options.C: Diagnosing the primary medical illness
options.D: Prescribing emergency surgical procedures

explanation: You got it! Accurate fluid charts help nurses catch dangerous fluid losses or fluid buildup early when bleeding, vomiting, or diarrhea strike. Essential nursing care! [learn more](GNS213_U3_T14#GNS213_U3_T14_h7)

question: What is a common misconception about advance care planning in healthcare?

options.A: That patients must pay a fee to create an advance directive
options.B: That doctors must approve every sentence written in a living will
options.C: That it is just a one-time signature on a legal form rather than an ongoing conversation
options.D: That nurses are legally forbidden from talking about living wills

explanation: Advance care planning is a continuous process of communication between patients, families, and providers, not just paperwork. [learn more](GNS221_U4_T7#GNS221_U4_T7_h5)

question: Why are patients told to avoid signing important legal documents for 24 hours after a sedated endoscopy?

options.A: Hospitals are legally liable for outside contracts signed.
options.B: Sedative drugs can temporarily impair judgment and memory.
options.C: The bright lights in the procedure room damage eye muscles.
options.D: Anesthesia causes permanent changes in logical thinking.

explanation: Even if they feel completely awake, leftover sedation affects clear thinking and memory, so making major choices can wait until the next day. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T2#GNS221_U2_T2_h8)

question: A nurse is teaching breathing techniques to a patient with severe lung fibrosis. Which method should the nurse demonstrate to help ease shortness of breath?

options.A: Holding the breath for two minutes after each deep sigh
options.B: Breathing exclusively through the mouth while running fast
options.C: Rapid shallow panting to increase carbon dioxide retention
options.D: Pursed-lip breathing to help keep airways open longer

explanation: Pursed-lip breathing creates gentle backpressure in the airways, preventing them from collapsing prematurely and easing shortness of breath. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T8#GNS213_U2_T8_h6)

question: Why is having a wide base of support important when standing or lifting?

options.A: It keeps blood flowing to the legs
options.B: It improves overall stability and balance
options.C: It increases the strength of arm muscles
options.D: It stops the patient from feeling dizzy

explanation: A wide base of support, with feet apart, helps keep the body balanced and prevents falls or strains. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T25#GNS222_U1_T25_h4)

question: Which of the following is NOT a typical mild side effect experienced during a GTT?

options.A: Sudden high fever and chills
options.B: Mild dizziness or lightheadedness
options.C: Sweating and feeling shaky
options.D: Nausea and stomach cramping

explanation: Fever and chills are signs of infection, not side effects of consuming a glucose solution. [learn more](GNS222_U2_T20#GNS222_U2_T20_h8)

question: What does equity mean in the context of primary health care?

options.A: Only wealthy individuals pay for health services
options.B: Essential health services are accessible to everyone
options.C: Doctors earn the same salary as community health workers
options.D: Every clinic has the exact same amount of money

explanation: Equity ensures fair distribution of health services so that all members of the community can access the care they need, regardless of financial standing. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T10#GNS112_U5_T10_h2)

question: When is it appropriate for a nurse to stop performing CPR?

options.A: When trained medical help arrives and takes over care
options.B: When family members ask the team to take a break
options.C: As soon as the nurse feels physically tired and sweaty
options.D: After five minutes of continuous compressions without a pulse

explanation: CPR continues until the patient recovers, professionals take over, or clear signs of death appear. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T1#GNS212_U2_T1_h8)

question: What can happen if severe, constant pregnancy heartburn is left completely untreated?

options.A: Inflammation and damage to the lining of the esophagus
options.B: Permanent hardening of the muscular stomach walls
options.C: Complete blockage of the upper respiratory airway
options.D: Sudden loss of all maternal digestive enzymes

explanation: Constant acid wash irritates and damages the delicate lining of the food pipe over time, leading to inflammation. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T013#GNS226_U2_T013_h7)

question: Which two hormones does the anterior pituitary gland release to directly stimulate the ovaries?

options.A: FSH and LH
options.B: Estrogen and progesterone
options.C: Prolactin and cortisol
options.D: GnRH and oxytocin

explanation: Follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH) and luteinizing hormone (LH) are the dynamic duo released by the pituitary gland to wake up the ovaries and get things moving. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T6#GNS311_U1_T6_h2)

question: What does a regular B-Mode ultrasound show you on the screen?

options.A: A bright color map of bone strength
options.B: A two-dimensional greyscale picture of internal organs
options.C: A live wave graph of the heart's electrical rhythm
options.D: A 3D heat map of the body's temperature

explanation: Think of B-Mode as your standard black-and-white anatomical view that outlines the shape and structure of organs. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T11#GNS123_U2_T11_h3)

question: Why are regular debriefing sessions important for palliative care nurses?

options.A: They replace the need for personal time off and vacation days
options.B: They are required by hospital administrators to track daily task completion
options.C: They punish nurses who make clinical errors during patient shifts
options.D: They provide a safe space to process difficult emotional experiences with peers

explanation: Debriefing allows nurses to share their heavy experiences, reduce stress, and prevent burnout through collective support. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T6#GNS321_U4_T6_h8)

question: Which complication is a primary concern during the vaginal delivery of a macrosomic infant born to a mother with diabetes?

options.A: Shoulder dystocia
options.B: Placental accreta
options.C: Uterine inversion
options.D: Rapid cervical closure

explanation: Macrosomia means the baby is very large, which frequently leads to the baby's shoulders getting stuck behind the maternal pubic bone during delivery. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T006#GNS226_U4_T006_h6)

question: Why is accurate timing and documentation following a cardiac arrest event so crucial?

options.A: It replaces the need for a verbal handover to the intensive care unit
options.B: It guarantees insurance payment for hospital equipment used
options.C: It is required only if the resuscitation attempt was completely successful
options.D: It provides a clear legal and clinical record of the emergency timeline

explanation: Detailed notes record the exact interventions and timing, which helps evaluate patient outcomes and guide future care. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T1#GNS212_U2_T1_h8)

question: Which sign in an enlarged lymph node strongly points toward cancer (malignancy)?

options.A: Soft, tender, and mobile
options.B: Small, rubbery, and painful
options.C: Hard, fixed, and painless
options.D: Warm, pulsating, and soft

explanation: Cancerous lymph nodes are typically firm or hard, stuck tightly in place (fixed), and usually don't hurt when you press them. [learn more](GNS311_U2_T3#GNS311_U2_T3_h4)

question: Why is it so important to keep pauses in chest compressions as short as possible when using an AED?

options.A: Pauses reduce blood flow to the heart and brain, lowering survival rates.
options.B: Pauses allow the patient's body temperature to drop too quickly.
options.C: Pauses confuse the AED computer and prevent rhythm analysis.
options.D: Pauses cause the AED battery to drain faster during the rescue.

explanation: Every second you stop pumping, blood stops flowing to the brain. Keeping compressions continuous gives the patient the best fighting chance. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T13#GNS212_U4_T13_h4)

question: What are the tiny clumps of bacteria and blood clots that form on heart valves in endocarditis called?

options.A: Thromboemboli
options.B: Vegetations
options.C: Aneurysms
options.D: Atheromas

explanation: These little clumps are called vegetations. They form when germs and tiny blood clots (platelets and fibrin) stick together on a damaged heart valve. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T6#GNS213_U1_T6_h2)

question: What is the key difference between formative and summative evaluation?

options.A: Formative evaluates financial budgets, while summative evaluates clinical nursing procedures.
options.B: Formative happens during the program for adjustments, while summative happens at the end to measure total impact.
options.C: Formative is performed by external auditors, while summative is done by community patients.
options.D: Formative measures individual patient recovery, while summative measures nationwide economics.

explanation: Easy to remember: Formative happens *during* the program to help you fix things on the fly. Summative happens *at the end* to see how well it all worked. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T1#GNS225_U2_T1_h6)

question: Why must you shake a suspension bottle vigorously right before pouring a dose?

options.A: To cool down the liquid inside the glass container
options.B: To evenly redistribute settled solid drug particles
options.C: To check if the outer safety seal is broken
options.D: To create air bubbles that make the drug taste better

explanation: Shaking mixes the active medicine back into the liquid so the patient gets the right dose, not just flavored water! [learn more](GNS122_U1_T21#GNS122_U1_T21_h4)

question: Which sign strongly points to a uterine infection instead of normal side effects?

options.A: Nausea that goes away in a day
options.B: Chills lasting only for the first two hours
options.C: Foul-smelling vaginal discharge and persistent fever
options.D: Cramping that feels worse than a normal period

explanation: Bad-smelling discharge and a fever that sticks around past day one are classic warning signs of infection like endometritis. Good to spot early! [learn more](GNS226_U5_T013#GNS226_U5_T013_h7)

question: What symptom does a patient classically feel during an aortic dissection?

options.A: A dull, aching pain in the calf muscle while walking
options.B: Sudden, severe tearing or ripping pain in the chest or back
options.C: Numbness and color changes in fingers during cold weather
options.D: Swelling and brownish discoloration around the ankles

explanation: An aortic dissection is terrifying because the inner layer of the aorta actually tears open, letting blood tunnel between the layers of the wall. Patients describe it as a violent 'ripping' sensation. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T10#GNS213_U1_T10_h6)

question: What happens immediately when a blood vessel is injured?

options.A: Smooth muscle in the vessel wall undergoes a vascular spasm
options.B: White blood cells rush to destroy the vessel walls
options.C: Red blood cells multiply rapidly in the local area
options.D: Large amounts of fibrin are immediately produced

explanation: The very first response to blood vessel damage is the contraction of smooth muscle to instantly narrow the vessel and reduce blood loss. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T3#GNS111_U2_T3_h2)

question: A nurse who has lost several patients recently starts feeling numb, irritable, and dreads going to work. What is the most effective nursing action?

options.A: Ignore the feelings because nurses must always stay tough
options.B: Work extra shifts to distract the mind from feeling sad
options.C: Talk about feelings in a staff debriefing and prioritize self-care
options.D: Change clinical departments without telling anyone

explanation: Sharing feelings with peers and practicing self-care helps nurses process stress and recover from compassion fatigue. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T8#GNS321_U4_T8_h8)

question: Why is rotating the application site essential when a patient uses transdermal patches?

options.A: To ensure the old patch stays stuck to the body for extra dosing
options.B: To prevent skin irritation, breakdown, and altered drug absorption
options.C: To force the medication to travel through different liver pathways
options.D: To stop the patient from forgetting where the patch was placed last week

explanation: Applying patches to the exact same spot repeatedly damages the skin barrier and can change how effectively the drug absorbs into the body. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T16#GNS125_U3_T16_h8)

question: Why might a severely anemic patient NOT show a blue skin color (cyanosis) even when their oxygen is dangerously low?

options.A: Their skin is naturally thicker and hides color changes better
options.B: Anemia causes the blood vessels to dilate and turn the skin red instead
options.C: They do not have enough red blood cells or hemoglobin to display the blue color
options.D: Their lungs absorb extra oxygen from the surrounding air

explanation: You're getting the hang of it! Cyanosis needs enough hemoglobin (the stuff in red blood cells that carries oxygen) to show that blue tint. If a patient is severely anemic, they simply don't have enough to show the color! [learn more](GNS213_U2_T10#GNS213_U2_T10_h5)

question: As a nurse, what crucial counseling point must you share with a client choosing natural family planning?

options.A: The calendar method works best for women with unpredictable cycles
options.B: Basal body temperature can replace barrier methods for infection control
options.C: These methods do not protect against sexually transmitted infections
options.D: Charting must be done only once a week to prevent stress

explanation: Always remind patients: natural family planning only helps with birth control. It offers zero protection against STIs—condoms are still needed for that! [learn more](GNS226_U6_T010#GNS226_U6_T010_h5)

question: Why do we keep the head of the bed elevated at thirty degrees for a client with a brain injury or altered consciousness?

options.A: To prevent the patient from falling out of bed
options.B: To promote venous drainage and help lower intracranial pressure
options.C: To completely eliminate the need for oral hygiene
options.D: To make it easier for family members to feed the patient

explanation: Keeping the head up uses gravity to help blood drain away from the brain, which keeps pressure inside the skull nice and low. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T6#GNS222_U3_T6_h6)

question: What is the very first thing you should do before making any hospital bed?

options.A: Strip all the old linens off the mattress simultaneously
options.B: Lock the bed wheels and adjust it to a comfortable working height
options.C: Ask the patient to stand up and walk around the ward
options.D: Remove all pillows and place them on a nearby chair

explanation: Correct! Safety first: lock the wheels so the bed doesn't roll away, and raise it so you don't hurt your back while working. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T3#GNS112_U4_T3_h6)

question: If a patient catches Hepatitis C from a poorly sterilized procedure, what long-term organ damage are they most at risk for?

options.B: Chronic liver damage and cirrhosis
options.C: Chronic respiratory failure and asthma
options.D: Permanent paralysis of the lower limbs

explanation: You got it! Hepatitis C attacks the liver, often causing long-term inflammation and scarring over time. Protecting patients from bloodborne infections is a huge part of our job. [learn more](GNS122_U4_T2#GNS122_U4_T2_h5)

question: Which part of the body naturally produces cortisol?

options.A: Thyroid gland
options.B: Adrenal cortex
options.C: Pancreatic islets
options.D: Posterior pituitary

explanation: Cortisol is a natural stress hormone made and released by the outer layer of your adrenal glands, called the adrenal cortex. You've got this! [learn more](GNS223_U7_T4#GNS223_U7_T4_h1)

question: Why is having a skilled birth attendant present during delivery so important?

options.A: They make antenatal visits unnecessary
options.B: They can quickly spot and manage emergencies like heavy bleeding
options.C: They guarantee the baby won't cry at birth
options.D: They prevent the mother from feeling any contractions

explanation: Exactly! Skilled attendants have the training to handle sudden delivery complications and save lives before things get out of hand. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T004#GNS226_U1_T004_h4)

question: Why are vitamins and minerals called essential micronutrients?

options.A: The human liver can easily manufacture them if the diet lacks variety.
options.B: They are the main source of daily calories and tissue bulk in the diet.
options.C: They are only needed during times of severe illness or physical injury.
options.D: The body needs them in small amounts and cannot produce enough on its own.

explanation: Brilliant! 'Micro' means we only need tiny amounts, but 'essential' means our bodies can't make them—so we must get them from our food. Easy peasy! [learn more](GNS215_U6_T9#GNS215_U6_T9_h1)

question: In Vroom's Expectancy Theory, what does the term 'valence' mean?

options.B: The physical effort required for a clinical task
options.C: The guarantee that a reward will be delivered
options.D: The value an individual places on a specific reward

explanation: Valence is simply how much you actually want or care about the reward being offered. If management offers a prize you don't care about, your valence is low! [learn more](GST321_U3_T6#GST321_U3_T6_h3)

question: How does hematogenous osteomyelitis differ from contiguous osteomyelitis?

options.A: Hematogenous only affects the skull, while contiguous affects long bones exclusively
options.B: Hematogenous is caused by viruses, whereas contiguous is always caused by fungi
options.C: Hematogenous spreads through the bloodstream, while contiguous comes from a nearby open wound or infection
options.D: Hematogenous occurs only in older adults, while contiguous is strictly pediatric

explanation: Think of 'hematogenous' as hitching a ride through the blood from somewhere else in the body, while 'contiguous' means the infection touched the bone directly from an outside wound nearby. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T18#GNS222_U1_T18_h2)

question: In the FAST stroke assessment tool, what does the letter 'T' stand for?

options.A: Temperature of the patient's skin
options.B: Tremors in the fingers and hands
options.C: Total paralysis of the lower limbs
options.D: Time to call emergency services

explanation: Time is brain! The 'T' reminds us to call for emergency help immediately when stroke signs appear, because quick action saves brain tissue. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T24#GNS222_U3_T24_h3)

question: What are the two major parts that make up the human nervous system?

options.A: Spinal cord and vertebral column
options.B: Sympathetic and parasympathetic systems
options.C: Central and peripheral nervous systems
options.D: Brain and cranial nerves

explanation: Spot on! The nervous system splits into two main teams: the central nervous system (your brain and spinal cord) and the peripheral nervous system (all the nerves branching out to the rest of your body). [learn more](GNS222_U3_T13#GNS222_U3_T13_h1)

question: What is the main sign of the bargaining stage?

options.A: Directing intense rage at doctors and family members
options.B: Completely accepting the diagnosis without any sorrow
options.C: Isolating oneself from all hospital staff and visitors
options.D: Attempting to negotiate for more time or less pain

explanation: In this stage, patients try to make a 'deal'—often with God or fate—to buy a little more time. [learn more](GNS221_U4_T3#GNS221_U4_T3_h4)

question: When would you choose a face mask instead of a nasal cannula for oxygen delivery?

options.A: When the patient only requires a very low flow rate of oxygen

options.C: When the patient is completely free of any respiratory distress
options.D: When the patient needs higher and more precise oxygen concentrations

question: What is a 'windshield survey' in community nursing?

options.A: Checking vehicle exhaust fumes to measure air pollution levels

options.C: Testing the driving vision of commercial vehicle drivers
options.D: Administering a written questionnaire to hospital patients

question: What is the primary goal of a physiotherapist working with an older adult?

options.A: Reviewing daily prescription drug charts for errors
options.B: Assisting with feeding during meal times
options.C: Providing emotional counseling for depression
options.D: Improving mobility, strength, and balance to prevent falls

explanation: Physiotherapists use guided exercises and movement training to help older adults stay steady, strong, and safe from falls. [learn more](GNS321_U3_T7#GNS321_U3_T7_h4)

question: Why should nurses separate the concepts of 'sex' and 'gender'?

options.A: It removes the need to collect demographic data during patient admission
options.B: It ensures that patients are only treated based on their chromosome count
options.C: It helps identify which health issues stem from biology versus societal rules
options.D: It proves that biological traits change more quickly than cultural norms

explanation: Separating them helps you see the whole picture. Some health problems happen because of our biology, while others happen because of society's rules and expectations for men and women. [learn more](GNS312_U4_T5#GNS312_U4_T5_h1)

question: Besides body movement, what is another vital function of skeletal muscle?

options.A: Regulating blood pH through bicarbonate storage
options.B: Filtering metabolic waste products from the blood
options.C: Producing red blood cells for oxygen transport
options.D: Generating body heat to maintain core temperature

question: In health informatics, what does the abbreviation CPOE stand for?

options.A: Certified Practical Operations Expert

options.D: Clinical Patient Online Evaluation

question: A patient with heart failure needs an IV infusion. What is your most important pre-infusion check?

question: What simple home care helps most with scrotal swelling on the first day after surgery?

options.A: Massaging the scrotum gently to drain excess fluid

options.D: Applying a firm heating pad directly to the skin

question: What is the primary purpose of bereavement support after a patient passes away?

options.A: To disinfect the hospital room according to policy
options.B: To complete hospital discharge billing procedures quickly

question: How should you position an adult patient's ear before using a tympanic thermometer?

question: What does 'informed choice' truly mean in family planning counseling?

options.C: Clients must follow the cultural preferences of their local community.

question: A patient with a chronic blood disorder is stressed about overwhelming hospital bills and housing issues. Who should you involve in their care plan?

options.C: A hospital physiotherapist

question: What is the main focus of cancer epidemiology?

options.A: Testing new chemotherapy drugs in the laboratory
options.B: Studying cancer patterns and causes in populations

options.D: Providing daily bedside care to cancer patients

question: What is the best way to write down a skin problem in a patient's nursing chart?

options.A: Write the single word 'rash' to save precious time

options.C: Guess the exact disease name without checking physical signs

question: What is usually the main cause behind an idiosyncratic drug reaction?

options.A: Taking a medication past its expiry date
options.B: Inherited genetic differences in metabolism
options.C: Accidental double dosing by the patient
options.D: Mixing the drug with dairy products

question: Which common non-pain physical symptom frequently happens when patients take opioid pain meds?

question: Why is a water-soluble lubricant used instead of an oil-based jelly on the tube?

options.A: Water-soluble jelly permanently stiffens the plastic tube

options.C: Water-soluble jelly will not harm the lungs if accidentally inhaled

question: What directly causes pain (dolor) during an acute inflammation?

options.A: Rapid freezing of the skin cells surrounding the wound

options.C: Direct destruction of the spinal cord by white blood cells
options.D: Pressure from swelling and chemicals irritating nerve endings

question: You check a preliminary scan report on a confused patient and discover an unexpected fracture. What is your best next step?

options.A: Notify the primary care provider or medical team immediately for follow-up orders
options.B: Place the patient in strict isolation to prevent further bone damage
options.C: Discharge the patient quickly before the family sees the report
options.D: Wait until the patient complains of severe pain before telling anyone

explanation: Quick communication is key! Letting the medical team know right away ensures the patient gets proper care and treatment for that surprise injury. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T5#GNS222_U1_T5_h8)

question: A doctor prescribes a proton pump inhibitor to a patient with a stomach ulcer. What is the goal of this medicine?

options.A: Reduced stomach acid production to promote ulcer healing
options.B: Increased release of bile to speed up fat digestion
options.C: Stimulation of the vagus nerve to increase appetite
options.D: Enhanced production of mucus by goblet cells

explanation: By shutting down those acid pumps, the stomach environment becomes less acidic, giving the sore tissue a chance to rest and heal up nicely. [learn more](GNS121_U1_T12#GNS121_U1_T12_h7)

question: Why must you warn a patient who just used a numbing mouthwash (like viscous lidocaine) to be careful before eating?

options.A: Lidocaine permanently destroys the taste buds on the tongue
options.B: The medication reacts badly with food and causes severe nausea
options.C: Swallowing the numbing agent stops stomach digestion completely
options.D: Numbing the mouth can lead to accidental biting or choking

explanation: When the mouth is numb, patients can easily bite their cheeks or tongue by mistake, or even choke on their food. Safety first! [learn more](GNS213_U3_T4#GNS213_U3_T4_h5)

question: A client with severe difficulty swallowing (dysphagia) just finished a meal in bed. What is your most important immediate action?

options.A: Brush the client's teeth while they lie flat on their back
options.B: Lay the client flat immediately to help with digestion
options.C: Keep the head of the bed elevated for at least 30 minutes
options.D: Encourage the client to drink a large glass of thin water quickly

explanation: Keeping the head elevated prevents food or liquid from flowing back up and entering the airway, which lowers the risk of choking or aspiration. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T15#GNS222_U4_T15_h6)

question: What does the abbreviation 'PO' mean on a drug chart?

options.A: By rectum
options.B: By mouth
options.C: Intravenously
options.D: Under the tongue

explanation: Well done! 'PO' stands for 'per os', a Latin phrase meaning by mouth. It's one of the most common routes you'll administer medications. [learn more](GNS125_U2_T8#GNS125_U2_T8_h3)

question: What is the time frame for defining puerperal sepsis following childbirth?

options.A: Strictly during the active stage of labor
options.B: Within the first 42 days postpartum
options.C: Between 6 weeks and 3 months postpartum
options.D: Only during the first 24 hours postpartum

explanation: Puerperal sepsis is officially defined as an infection of the genital tract occurring anytime from the onset of membrane rupture or labor up to 42 days following delivery. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T024#GNS226_U3_T024_h1)

question: Which sign points strongly to a wound infection after a skin biopsy?

options.A: A thin line of pink tissue along the suture line
options.B: Temporary numbness fading after the local anesthetic wears off
options.C: Spreading redness, warmth, and purulent drainage
options.D: Mild itching around the edges of the adhesive bandage

question: Which of these best describes a quality improvement framework in action?

options.A: Punishing staff members immediately whenever a patient complains about waiting times

options.C: Hiding poor treatment outcomes from hospital management to avoid criticism
options.D: Stopping all routine data collection until the end of the calendar year

explanation: You got it! Quality improvement is all about looking at data, spotting problems, and testing little tweaks to see what makes patient care better. [learn more](GNS312_U5_T2#GNS312_U5_T2_h7)

question: A doctor wants to know if a patient's low testosterone is due to a problem in the testes or the pituitary gland. Which test helps figure this out?

options.A: Serum LH and FSH hormone levels
options.B: A prostate-specific antigen blood test
options.C: A complete blood count with differential
options.D: A routine urinalysis and urine culture

explanation: Checking LH and FSH levels from the pituitary gland helps doctors see if the issue starts in the brain (pituitary) or down in the testes. Excellent clinical thinking! [learn more](GNS311_U1_T13#GNS311_U1_T13_h6)

question: What does the intraarticular route of medication administration involve?

options.A: Delivering drugs through the skin using a patch
options.B: Swallowing pills for systemic joint relief
options.C: Administering medicine into a muscle belly
options.D: Injecting medication directly into a joint space

explanation: Intraarticular simply means putting the drug straight inside the joint cavity. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T9#GNS125_U3_T9_h1)

question: What is an important long-term instruction for a patient who just received a mechanical heart valve?

options.A: Never drinking pure water again
options.B: Avoiding all forms of physical movement forever
options.C: Stopping daily blood pressure checks at home
options.D: The need for lifelong anticoagulation therapy

explanation: Blood loves to stick to artificial surfaces! Patients with mechanical valves must take blood thinners (anticoagulants) for the rest of their lives to prevent dangerous clots. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T5#GNS213_U1_T5_h10)

question: A family asks to perform a special prayer ritual at the bedside that slightly changes the visiting routine. What should you do?

options.A: Tell the family they must perform their prayers outside the building
options.B: Refuse the request immediately to avoid breaking hospital rules
options.C: Ignore the family and proceed with normal nursing tasks
options.D: Accommodate the request respectfully and find a safe compromise

explanation: As long as it's safe, always respect cultural and spiritual wishes—it's a vital part of compassionate end-of-life care. [learn more](GNS221_U4_T8#GNS221_U4_T8_h6)

question: What is the medical term for abnormally heavy or prolonged menstrual bleeding?

options.A: Oligomenorrhea
options.B: Dysmenorrhea
options.C: Menorrhagia
options.D: Amenorrhea

explanation: Menorrhagia describes periods that are excessively heavy or last longer than normal, often draining the body's iron stores. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T10#GNS311_U1_T10_h2)

question: What is the first and most effective step to control external bleeding from a limb wound?

options.A: Applying a loose gauze wrap for comfort
options.B: Massaging the muscles above the injury
options.C: Pouring cold water over the injured area
options.D: Applying direct pressure to the wound

question: What standard unit of measurement is used on a hospital fluid intake and output chart?

question: What is the golden rule for traction weights on a patient's bed?

options.C: Lift the weights manually during every nursing shift change

question: Why must nurses care about how medications are stored on the ward?

options.A: Pharmaceutical companies only trust nurses with liquid medications
options.B: Hospital pharmacists do not understand basic ward temperature needs
options.C: Nurses handle drugs from the supply point to actual bedside administration
options.D: The law requires nurses to manufacture all ward level supplies

explanation: Spot on! You are the crucial link between the pharmacy and the patient's bedside, making drug safety a key part of your daily care. [learn more](GNS125_U4_T4#GNS125_U4_T4_h1)

question: When should a nurse document that a medication has been given to a patient?

options.D: Whenever the nurse has spare time during the day

explanation: Documenting right after administration prevents accidental double-dosing and ensures an accurate, up-to-date medical record. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T2#GNS122_U1_T2_h8)

question: Why must an unconscious patient be turned to their side when you are cleaning their mouth?

question: Why is it important for nurses to report both real vaccine reactions and random health events that happen after vaccination?

question: Why do clinical departments use standardized grading rubrics (marking guides) for procedures?

question: Which key principle says that local people must be involved in planning their own health programs?

question: Why would a doctor order a 24-hour Holter monitor for a patient with occasional dizzy spells?

question: When are transmission-based precautions added to patient care?

question: A patient is admitted for monitoring after receiving a dose of methotrexate. Which nursing intervention is most important during her hospital stay?

question: A 40-year-old client with a desk job and a high body weight asks about their risk for diabetes. What is the best nursing explanation?

question: What crucial equipment must be kept right at the bedside after a thyroid surgery?

question: What usually happens during the orientation phase of meeting a patient?

question: A pregnant client shares that she drank a local root mix to prevent pregnancy before realizing she was already conceiving. How should you respond?

options.B: Assess for any adverse side effects and provide supportive prenatal guidance

question: Why must a nurse stay at the bedside until the patient swallows all their medications?

question: Why is pricing drugs based on old historical costs dangerous during high inflation?

question: Which of these is a key focus during Antenatal Care (ANC) visits in Nigerian clinics?

question: Which medication is a core part of the preferred first-line ART treatment for adults in Nigeria?

question: If a patient has a stroke on the right side of their motor cortex, which side of the body will show physical weakness?

question: Why is wearing a face shield so important when you are about to drain an abscess?

question: What is the medical word for when a patient is taking many different medications at the same time?

question: What crucial nursing check must be done before giving food or water to a stroke patient who might have trouble swallowing?

options.B: A measurement of 24-hour urine output
options.C: A formal bedside swallow screen

question: When is the absolute best time for a patient to apply moisturizing creams (emollients)?

question: Why is a smaller bump size (5 mm) counted as positive for patients living with HIV?

question: How should you communicate updates to the worried family of a critically ill patient?

question: A patient after surgery has a swollen tummy, has not passed gas, and you hear zero bowel sounds. What condition do you suspect?

question: A nurse has just placed a warm poultice on a patient's leg. When is the best time to check the skin underneath for irritation?

question: Why is suddenly stopping long-term steroid therapy so dangerous (leading to an addisonian crisis)?

options.C: The adrenal glands have atrophied and cannot immediately produce natural cortisol

question: When taking off dirty gloves, where should your very first move begin?

question: What is the highest score a patient can get on the eye-opening part of the GCS?

question: Why is the cricoid cartilage so important in emergency airway procedures?

question: Why is the first sixty minutes after a major injury famously called the 'golden hour'?

question: Where does the circulating nurse work during a surgical procedure?

question: A patient comes in with swollen lower legs, brownish skin around the ankles, and a dull ache that gets worse when standing. What condition is most likely?

options.A: Raynaud's disease
options.B: Acute arterial blockage
options.C: Chronic venous insufficiency
options.D: Severe peripheral arterial disease

explanation: Those brownish marks, swelling, and tired aching legs are classic signs that blood is pooling in the lower legs because the veins are struggling to push it back up. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T11#GNS213_U1_T11_h3)

question: Why would a doctor request serum electrolyte tests for a patient with severe vomiting and diarrhea?

options.A: To check for dangerous mineral losses like sodium and potassium
options.B: To measure how fast the stomach lining is healing itself
options.C: To check if the patient has developed a food allergy
options.D: To determine the exact species of virus causing the infection

explanation: Frequent fluid loss depletes essential body salts, and blood tests help guide safe intravenous or oral electrolyte replacement. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T20#GNS313_U2_T20_h4)

question: What is the main feature of polycythaemia?

options.A: A dangerous drop in blood platelets
options.B: A sudden drop in white blood cells
options.C: An abnormal increase in red blood cells
options.D: Too much fluid loss from blood vessels

explanation: You've got this! Polycythaemia simply means an overproduction of red blood cells in the body. [learn more](GNS311_U2_T8#GNS311_U2_T8_h1)

question: Which client should you, as a nurse, keep a close eye on for signs of complicated grief?

options.A: A client who cries openly while talking about a loved one during the first week after a death
options.B: A client who expresses persistent bitterness and an inability to accept a sudden loss many months later
options.C: A client who finds comfort in sharing memories of the deceased with close friends
options.D: A client who participates in traditional funeral and memorial services

explanation: Spot on! Holding onto deep bitterness and refusing to accept the reality months down the track are red flags for complicated grief. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T9#GNS321_U4_T9_h7)

question: What should a client do if she has sex again just four hours after putting in her diaphragm?

options.A: Apply more spermicide into the vagina without removing the diaphragm
options.B: Remove the diaphragm immediately and use an emergency oral contraceptive
options.C: Leave everything alone because the original spermicide is still active
options.D: Take the diaphragm out, wash it, and reinsert it with fresh spermicide

explanation: For repeat intercourse, she should just push more spermicide straight into the vagina without taking the device out. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T017#GNS226_U6_T017_h5)

question: A patient comes in feeling constantly exhausted, has gained weight, hates cold weather, and has dry, coarse hair. What condition do these signs point to?

options.A: Hypothyroidism
options.B: Hyperthyroidism
options.C: Cushing's syndrome
options.D: Addison's disease

explanation: You've got this! These are classic signs of a sluggish metabolism caused by not having enough thyroid hormones in the body. [learn more](GNS222_U2_T14#GNS222_U2_T14_h3)

question: Which of the following describes Type I FGM?

options.A: Cutting away both the clitoris and labia majora
options.B: Partial or total removal of the clitoris
options.C: Creating a seal over the vaginal opening
options.D: Piercing or scraping the labia majora

explanation: Type I focuses on removing part or all of the clitoris. You'll see this classification often in community health nursing! [learn more](GNS225_U6_T3#GNS225_U6_T3_h3)

question: What tells you that an infant is ready to come out of Gallows traction?

options.A: The baby turns two years old
options.B: The ropes are starting to look worn out
options.C: X-rays show the bone has healed well with good callus formation
options.D: The parents ask for the metal frame to be taken down

explanation: We don't guess—we check! Only an X-ray proving the bone is strong enough will greenlight removing the traction. [learn more](GNS221_U1_T10#GNS221_U1_T10_h7)

question: A patient wants to eat more fiber without getting severe gas and bloating. What advice should you give?

options.A: Introduce high-fiber foods slowly so the digestive system can adapt over time.
options.B: Take strong laxatives with every single meal containing fiber.
options.C: Stop eating all forms of fiber completely to avoid any digestive effort.
options.D: Eat a massive amount of beans and raw vegetables all at once on day one.

explanation: Slow and steady wins the race! Giving the gut time to adjust to fiber prevents sudden cramps and gas. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T10#GNS212_U1_T10_h7)

question: When a female condom is inserted properly, where does its closed end sit?

options.A: Over the cervix
options.B: Around the base of the bladder
options.C: Against the labia majora
options.D: Inside the fallopian tube

explanation: You got it! The closed end goes deep inside to rest right over the cervix, much like a diaphragm does. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T016#GNS226_U6_T016_h2)

question: What is the specific job of misoprostol during a medical abortion?

options.A: It blocks the action of progesterone in the uterine lining
options.B: It causes uterine contractions to expel the pregnancy tissue
options.C: It prevents nausea caused by the breakdown of the decidua
options.D: It stops heavy bleeding by constricting pelvic blood vessels

explanation: Great job! Misoprostol is a prostaglandin that tells the smooth muscles of the uterus to contract and gently push out the tissue. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T012#GNS226_U5_T012_h2)

question: What is the primary hormone secreted by the hypothalamus that starts the reproductive hormone chain?

options.A: Follicle-stimulating hormone
options.B: Luteinizing hormone
options.C: Gonadotropin-releasing hormone
options.D: Testosterone

explanation: The hypothalamus releases gonadotropin-releasing hormone to trigger the pituitary gland, which drives the entire reproductive hormone pathway. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T20#GNS312_U1_T20_h1)

question: Why does an intravenous (IV) medication work much faster than a swallowed pill?

options.A: It travels straight to the liver for immediate activation
options.B: It is manufactured using higher chemical concentrations
options.C: It avoids the lungs where oxygen slows down circulation
options.D: It enters the bloodstream directly without needing absorption

explanation: Exactly! Because IV meds skip the digestive tract and go straight into the blood, they start working almost instantly. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T1#GNS122_U1_T1_h4)

question: What should you do if your control solution test result falls way outside the normal range?

options.A: Use the meter on patients anyway and note the variance
options.B: Ignore the test because controls are unreliable
options.C: Add water to the control solution
options.D: Take the meter out of service and report it

explanation: If the control check fails, the system isn't reliable. Put it aside and report the equipment issue so patient safety isn't compromised. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T5#GNS212_U4_T5_h7)

question: What distinct shape do the ulcers formed by this parasite in the colon usually take?

options.A: Circular crater ulcers
options.B: Flask-shaped ulcers
options.C: Linear strip ulcers
options.D: Raised button ulcers

explanation: You got it! As the parasites burrow into the gut lining, they carve out classic flask-shaped sores. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T21#GNS313_U2_T21_h3)

question: Why might a pulse oximeter reading look completely normal in someone with carbon monoxide poisoning?

options.A: Carbon monoxide stimulates the lungs to hyperventilate, boosting true oxygen.
options.B: Pulse oximeters often mistake carboxyhemoglobin for oxygenated hemoglobin.
options.C: Carbon monoxide physically increases the total amount of dissolved oxygen in plasma.
options.D: The device only measures heart rate and fails to detect blood gas saturation.

explanation: Standard pulse oximgs can't tell the difference between oxygen and carbon monoxide attached to hemoglobin. It gives a falsely reassuring reading even when the patient is in danger—so always look at the clinical picture! [learn more](GNS112_U7_T5#GNS112_U7_T5_h4)

question: How do nurses accurately measure fluid output from a heavy surgical dressing or pad?

options.A: Estimating the stain size using a common ruler
options.B: Squeezing the fluid out into a measuring cup
options.C: Asking the patient how much fluid they think leaked
options.D: Weighing the wet item and subtracting the dry weight

explanation: Weight is the most reliable way to quantify fluid soaked into solid materials, where one gram roughly equals one milliliter. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T19#GNS122_U1_T19_h5)

question: What is the difference between withholding and withdrawing medical treatment?

options.A: Withholding is illegal, while withdrawing is legally permitted
options.B: There is no difference in definition, only in the cost of medications
options.C: Withholding requires court approval, while withdrawing requires only family consent
options.D: Withholding means never starting an intervention, while withdrawing means stopping an ongoing one

explanation: It's all about timing! Withholding means you decide not to start a treatment in the first place, while withdrawing means you turn off or stop a treatment that was already running. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T7#GNS321_U4_T7_h4)
